description:
src/filenode.rs:604-621: when onDestroyRemoveChildren=false, the handler calls get_descendant_ids(id) and then computes 'all_covered = desc_ids.iter().all(|did| destroy_id_set.contains(did))'.

This is mostly right, but get_descendant_ids returns the TRANSITIVE descendant set (per the trait doc at src/backend.rs:85-87: 'all IDs that are descendants of the given node (children, grandchildren, etc.)'). The all_covered check then requires every transitive descendant to be in destroy_id_set.

The spec §3.2.3 lines 542-546 says: 'if all the child nodes are being destroyed in the same operation, then the server MUST NOT return this error. Servers MUST either sort the destroys children before parents, or only check this constraint on the final state.'

The current check correctly handles the parent-with-direct-children case but does not handle the partial-tree case: a destroy set { A, B } where A is the root, B is A's child, and B has its own child C that is NOT in the destroy set. get_descendant_ids(A) returns {B, C}; destroy_id_set = {A, B}; all_covered is false; nodeHasChildren is correctly returned for A.

However, consider get_descendant_ids(B): it returns {C}; destroy_id_set = {A, B}; all_covered for B is false; nodeHasChildren is returned for B too. The handler reports notDestroyed for both A and B, even though the user's intent (destroy parent and all its descendants) is consistent and the spec mandates returning nodeHasChildren only on a final-state basis.

The current behavior may be acceptable (it never falsely succeeds), but two issues:

1. The error attribution is suboptimal: nodeHasChildren is reported on B, not on the actual descendant C that is the root cause.
2. There is no test covering this partial-tree case, so a future refactor that reorders the destroys could regress.

Required: clarify with a test the multi-level destroy_id_set case and either (a) attribute the error to the deepest uncovered descendant, or (b) clearly document the current 'each level checks its own subtree' behavior in the handler doc-comment.
title: destroy parent + all children check is correct only for direct same-depth recursion; multi-level children require transitive closure
